text:
maya: Heads-up — BigCorp renewal email dropped this morning. they want a 99.95% SLA + 50ms p95 for our hosted endpoint within the next quarter. can we talk tradeoffs? :eyes:
devin: whoa. do we have telemetry showing current p95 for their workload?
alisa: CS forwarded their perf traces. 120ms p95 on avg for their typical prompt sizes. they called this a deal blocker.
maya: high-level ask: decide if we pause Q2 roadmap slice and slot a focused perf sprint, or offer a tailored commercial SLA (higher price, dedicated pool) as a workaround.
tom: sales prefers a commercial SLA — keeps roadmap momentum and closes renewal. they can pay for dedicated capacity.
raj: dedicated pool buys latency but increases ops work and infra cost. also we need model variant + quantization validation for correctness at lower precision.
maya: can we do a quick RICE-style back of envelope? impact = renewal (~$900k ARR), reach = 1 customer, confidence = 60%, effort = 6 dev-weeks across infra/eng/qa.
devin: quick calc: RICE = (Impact*Reach*Confidence)/Effort. if we normalize impact to 9 (for big revenue), reach 1, conf 0.6 => 5.4/6 ~= 0.9 score. not great compared to multi-customer infra investments.
alisa: but renewal risk has downstream churn/case studies value. non-linear. losing them could hurt go-to-market cred.
maya: two options sketched: A) fast patch: scoped latency optimizations (batching tweaks, KV cache warmers, tuned kernels) — 3 weeks, minimal infra. B) Dedicated SLA: reserved pool + SLA + opt-in quantization testing — 8 weeks but revenue-covered.
raj: A reduces p95 maybe 20-30ms for some workloads. B is more certain to hit 50ms. A carries risk of rework for other customers.
devin: also need rollout criteria: measurable p95 drop in staging with their traces, no regression on hallucination/eval set. if either fails, fallback to dedicated offer.
maya: decision needed by EOD Friday for sales to present terms. thoughts?
tom: sales will accept either as long as we can give a clear timeline and a fallback commercial SLA. prefer B if we can commit 8 weeks.
alisa: CS can negotiate a staged commitment: short extension if we start A immediately and agree to move to B if metrics not met. that buys time.
raj: engineering preference: start A as quick experiment (2-3 ppl) and parallelize planning for B (infra + SRE + security review). budget-wise we need sign-off for dedicated infra costs.
maya: action items: 1) dev to run a focused perf run with BigCorp traces by Wed — devin + raj. 2) CS to offer staged timeline to customer by Thurs — alisa. 3) Sales to prepare draft contract language for dedicated SLA pricing — tom. 4) Product to sync on rollback/metrics and canary policy — maya.
planning-bot: Reminder: add task cards to #planning board and tag @finance for dedicated pool budget approval.
devin: I can get initial perf numbers by Wed EOD.
alisa: I'll draft the staged-extension email and share for review.
tom: will work pricing and get legal involved. targeting Thurs internal review.
maya: thanks — sync up tomorrow 10am. :thumbsup:
